questionText:
An application executes $6.4 \times 10^8$ number of instructions in $6.3$ seconds. There are four types of instructions, the details of which are given in the table. The duration of a clock cycle in nanoseconds is __________. (rounded off to one decimal place)

Instruction type Clock cycles required per instruction (CPI) Number of instructions executed
Branch 2 $2.25 \times 10^8$
Load 5 $1.20 \times 10^8$
Store 4 $1.65 \times 10^8$
Arithmetic 3 $1.30 \times 10^8$
explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the total number of clock cycles required.
Total Cycles = $\sum (\text{CPI}_i \times \text{Instruction Count}_i)$
Total Cycles = $(2 \times 2.25 \times 10^8) + (5 \times 1.20 \times 10^8) + (4 \times 1.65 \times 10^8) + (3 \times 1.30 \times 10^8)$
Total Cycles = $(4.50 + 6.00 + 6.60 + 3.90) \times 10^8 = 21.0 \times 10^8$ cycles.

Step 2: Calculate the duration of one clock cycle (Cycle Time).
Execution Time = Total Cycles $\times$ Cycle Time
$6.3 \text{ seconds} = 21.0 \times 10^8 \times \text{Cycle Time}$
Cycle Time = $\frac{6.3}{21.0 \times 10^8} = 0.3 \times 10^{-8} \text{ seconds} = 3 \times 10^{-9} \text{ seconds} = 3.0 \text{ ns}$.

Thus, the duration of a clock cycle is 3.0 nanoseconds.
